chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
The waiting period (iddah) of the woman who menstruates and whose menstruation is regular is three qur' (periods), and these are three hayd (menstrual periods).

key_terms.أَقْرَاءٍ: Plural of qur', referring to menstrual cycles or periods of purity between them.
key_terms.حِيَضٍ: Plural of hayd, referring to the actual menstrual bleeding periods.
key_terms.عِدَّةُ: Waiting period (Iddah), the period a woman must observe after divorce or death of husband before remarrying.

ai.seo_question: What is the duration of the iddah for a woman with regular menstruation according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the concept of 'qur'' is clarified not merely as a period of purity but specifically as three complete menstrual cycles, establishing a precise metric for the iddah of women with regular menstruation. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for determining the end of the waiting period following divorce or widowhood, emphasizing the biological reality of the cycle as the primary indicator. The hadith reflects the juristic principle of relying on observable physical signs to derive legal timelines, a key feature of Usuli methodology.
